verses.text: Korah son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, became proud. He was joined by Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, from the tribe of Reuben.
They rose up against Moses, together with two hundred fifty men of Israel, well-known leaders who had been chosen by the community.

They gathered against Moses and Aaron and said to them, "You have gone too far! The whole community is holy, every one of them, and the LORD is with them. So why do you put yourselves above the LORD's people?"
When Moses heard this, he bowed down with his face to the ground.

Then he said to Korah and all his followers, "In the morning the LORD will show who belongs to him and who is holy. He will let that person come near him. The one he chooses, he will bring near to himself.
So this is what you must do, Korah, you and all your followers: take incense pans.
Tomorrow, put fire and incense in them before the LORD. The man the LORD chooses will be the one who is holy. You Levites have gone too far!"
Moses also said to Korah, "Listen, you Levites!

Is it not enough for you that the God of Israel has set you apart from the rest of the community and brought you near to himself? He lets you work at the LORD's Holy Tent and stand before the community to serve them.
He has brought you and all your fellow Levites near to himself. Now you want to be priests too?
It is really against the LORD that you and all your followers have joined together. Who is Aaron, that you complain against him?"
Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab. But they said, "We will not come!
Is it not enough that you brought us out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the desert? Now you also want to make yourself our ruler!
You have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, or given us fields and vineyards to own. Do you think you can fool these men? We will not come!"
Moses became very angry and said to the LORD, "Do not accept their offering. I have not taken even one donkey from them, and I have never done wrong to any of them."
Moses said to Korah, "Tomorrow you and all your followers must stand before the LORD, you and they, and Aaron too.
Each man must take his incense pan and put incense in it. Bring them before the LORD, two hundred fifty incense pans. You and Aaron must bring your pans as well."
So each man took his incense pan, put fire and incense in it, and stood with Moses and Aaron at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
Korah gathered all his followers against them at the door of the Tent of Meeting. Then the glory of the LORD appeared to the whole community.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Move away from these people, so that I can destroy them at once!"
But Moses and Aaron bowed down with their faces to the ground and said, "O God, the God who gives breath to all living things, will you be angry with the whole community when only one man sins?"
Then the LORD said to Moses,
"Tell the community: 'Move away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.'"
Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the leaders of Israel followed him.
He warned the community, "Get away from the tents of these evil men! Do not touch anything that belongs to them, or you will be destroyed because of all their sins."

So the people moved away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram on every side. Dathan and Abiram had come out and were standing at the doors of their tents with their wives, their sons, and their little children.
Then Moses said, "This is how you will know that the LORD has sent me to do all these things, and that it was not my own idea.
If these men die a natural death, as all people die, then the LORD has not sent me.

But if the LORD does something completely new, and the ground opens up and swallows them with everything they own, and they go down alive to the place of the dead, then you will know that these men have rejected the LORD."
As soon as Moses finished saying all this, the ground under them split open.
The earth opened up and swallowed them and their families, all of Korah's men, and everything they owned.
They went down alive to the place of the dead, with everything they had. The earth closed over them, and they disappeared from the community.
All the people of Israel around them heard their screams and ran away, shouting, "The earth is going to swallow us too!"
Then fire came out from the LORD and burned up the two hundred fifty men who were offering the incense.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, to take the incense pans out of the fire and scatter the burning coals far away, because the pans are holy.

These are the pans of the men who sinned at the cost of their lives. Hammer them into thin sheets to cover the altar, because they were offered before the LORD and have become holy. They will be a warning sign to the people of Israel."
So Eleazar the priest collected the bronze incense pans brought by the men who had been burned up, and had them hammered into a covering for the altar.

This was a reminder to the people of Israel that no one except a descendant of Aaron should come to burn incense before the LORD, or he would become like Korah and his followers. This was just as the LORD had told Eleazar through Moses.
But the next day the whole community of Israel complained against Moses and Aaron. They said, "You have killed the LORD's people!"
When the community gathered against Moses and Aaron, they turned toward the Tent of Meeting, and suddenly the cloud covered it, and the glory of the LORD appeared.
Moses and Aaron went to the front of the Tent of Meeting.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Get away from these people, so that I can destroy them at once!" And they bowed down with their faces to the ground.

Moses said to Aaron, "Take your incense pan, put fire from the altar in it, and add incense. Hurry to the community and make them right with God. The LORD's anger has broken out, and the deadly disease has started."
Aaron did what Moses said. He ran into the middle of the crowd, where the disease had already begun among the people. He put the incense on and made the people right with God.
He stood between the dead and the living, and the disease stopped.
Fourteen thousand seven hundred people died from the disease, besides those who had died because of Korah.
Then Aaron went back to Moses at the door of the Tent of Meeting, because the disease had stopped.
